quote: Patients with a history of autoimmune disease and those who had received previous treatments with docetaxel, CD137 agonists, anti-CTLA4, or therapies targeting the PD-L1 and PD-1 pathway were excluded.
summary: CTLA4 appears only in trial exclusion criteria (prior anti-CTLA4 therapy) in a lung cancer atezolizumab trial; nothing on UC.

quote: In patients with melanoma, ipilimumab (an antibody against cytotoxic T-lymphocyte-associated antigen 4 [CTLA-4]) prolongs overall survival, and nivolumab (an antibody against the programmed death 1 [PD-1] receptor) produced durable tumor regression in a phase 1 trial.
summary: A melanoma trial of nivolumab plus ipilimumab (anti-CTLA-4); outcomes are tumour response and general adverse events, with no gene-specific inflammation or UC result.

quote: Most notable has been the ability of the anti-CTLA4 antibody, ipilimumab, to achieve a significant increase in survival for patients with metastatic melanoma, for which conventional therapies have failed.
summary: A cancer immunotherapy review noting anti-CTLA4 ipilimumab improved melanoma survival; no UC content.

quote: Tumors in antibiotic-treated or germ-free mice did not respond to CTLA blockade.
summary: In mice, anti-CTLA-4 antitumour efficacy depended on Bacteroides species in the gut microbiota; the outcome is tumour response, not colitis.

quote: The spectrum differed widely between regimens: in a total of 193 anti-CTLA-4 deaths, most were usually from colitis (135 [70%]), whereas anti-PD-1/PD-L1-related fatalities were often from pneumonitis (333 [35%]), hepatitis (115 [22%]), and neurotoxic effects (50 [15%]).
summary: In pharmacovigilance data, most fatal toxicity from anti-CTLA-4 blockade in cancer patients was colitis, so CTLA-4 inhibition can cause severe colitis.

quote: Treatment with both CTLA-4 and PD-1/PD-L1 blockade is associated with a unique pattern of adverse events called immune-related adverse events, and occasionally, unusual kinetics of tumor response are seen.
summary: A review of checkpoint blockade in cancer noting CTLA-4 blockade causes immune-related adverse events; no UC-specific data.

quote: Anti-CTLA4 predominantly inhibits T-regulatory cells (Treg cells), thereby increasing the CD8 T-cell to Treg (CD8/Treg) ratio.
summary: In mouse melanoma models, anti-CTLA4 inhibited Tregs and, with radiation and PD-L1 blockade, drove tumour regression; outcomes are tumour related, not colitis.

quote: Immune-checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs), including anti-cytotoxic T lymphocyte antigen 4 (CTLA-4), anti-programmed cell death 1 (PD-1) and anti-programmed cell death 1 ligand 1 (PD-L1) antibodies, are arguably the most important development in cancer therapy over the past decade.
summary: A review of immune-related adverse events of checkpoint inhibitors including anti-CTLA-4; CTLA-4 is not discussed on its own and UC is not covered.

quote: Checkpoint inhibitor-based immunotherapies that target cytotoxic T lymphocyte antigen 4 (CTLA4) or the programmed cell death 1 (PD1) pathway have achieved impressive success in the treatment of different cancer types.
summary: A review of biomarkers of response to CTLA4 and PD1 checkpoint inhibitors in cancer; no UC data.

quote: In vivo blockade of CTLA-4 for a limited period in normal mice leads to spontaneous development of chronic organ-specific autoimmune diseases, which are immunopathologically similar to human counterparts.
summary: Blocking CTLA-4 in normal mice triggers autoimmune disease and impairs regulatory T cell suppression, showing CTLA-4 maintains self-tolerance.

quote: Our studies reveal that the immune-suppressive function of these cells in vivo is dependent on signaling via the negative regulator of T cell activation cytotoxic T lymphocyte-associated antigen 4 (CTLA-4), as well as secretion of the immune-suppressive cytokine transforming growth factor beta.
summary: In mouse T cell transfer colitis, the ability of CD25+ regulatory T cells to control intestinal inflammation depends on CTLA-4 signalling.

quote: B7-dependent responses in Cd28(-/-)Ctla4(-/-) T cells together with reports of stimulatory and inhibitory functions for Programmed Death-1 Ligand 1 or 2 molecules (PD-L1 or PD-L2) have suggested additional receptors for these B7 family members.
summary: The paper is about PD-L1 binding B7-1; CTLA-4 is mainly a comparison binding partner and deficient-cell control, with no inflammation or colitis outcome.

quote: In recent times, more than four check point antibody inhibitors have been commercialized for targeting PD-1, PDL-1, and CTLA-4.
summary: A PD-1/PD-L1 cancer review mentions CTLA-4 only as another commercialised checkpoint target.

quote: Treatment with a selective PI3Kβ inhibitor improved the efficacy of both anti-PD-1 and anti-CTLA-4 antibodies in murine models.
summary: Anti-CTLA-4 antibody is one of the immunotherapies combined with a PI3Kbeta inhibitor in a melanoma PTEN-loss paper; no CTLA-4-specific inflammation result.

quote: We demonstrate, however, that the activity of anti-CTLA-4 antibody on the T reg cell compartment is mediated via selective depletion of T reg cells within tumor lesions.
summary: In mouse melanoma, anti-CTLA-4 acts by Fc-dependent depletion of tumour-infiltrating Tregs; the outcome is tumour response, not colitis.

quote: Among them, immune checkpoint inhibitors, which target PD-1, PD-L1 and CTLA-4, are increasingly used for certain cancers; however, this increased use has resulted in increased reports of immune-related adverse events (irAEs).
summary: A review of immune-related adverse events from checkpoint inhibitors including anti-CTLA-4; no gene-specific UC data.

quote: This blockade of CTLA-4 induced grade III/IV autoimmune manifestations in six patients (43%), including dermatitis, enterocolitis, hepatitis, and hypophysitis, and mediated objective cancer regression in three patients (21%; two complete and one partial responses).
summary: Anti-CTLA-4 antibody in melanoma patients caused severe autoimmune effects including enterocolitis, indicating CTLA-4 restrains autoimmunity and gut inflammation.

quote: In this study, we demonstrated that CD4(+)CD25(+) T cells do produce high levels of transforming growth factor (TGF)-beta1 and interleukin (IL)-10 compared with CD4(+)CD25(-) T cells when stimulated by plate-bound anti-CD3 and soluble anti-CD28 and/or IL-2, and secretion of TGF-beta1 (but not other cytokines), is further enhanced by costimulation via cytotoxic T lymphocyte-associated antigen (CTLA)-4.
summary: In vitro, CTLA-4 costimulation of regulatory T cells enhanced TGF-beta1 secretion; CTLA-4 is a minor aspect of a paper on TGF-beta-mediated suppression.

quote: These include rashes, which may rarely progress to life-threatening toxic epidermal necrolysis, and colitis, characterized by a mild to moderate, but occasionally also severe and persistent diarrhea.
summary: A review of managing immune-related adverse events, including colitis, from anti-CTLA-4 ipilimumab in cancer patients; no new data.

quote: Among these immunotherapies, neutralizing antibodies targeting the immune checkpoints T-lymphocyte-associated protein 4 (CTLA-4) and programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) are being hailed as particularly successful.
summary: A review of mechanisms and limitations of anti-PD-1 and anti-CTLA-4 therapy in melanoma; no UC content.

quote: Only stimulation of T cells with mature DCs resulted in an upregulation of CD154, CD69, and CD70, whereas T cells activated with immature DCs showed an early upregulation of the negative regulator cytotoxic T lymphocyte-associated molecule 4 (CTLA-4).
summary: Human T cells stimulated by immature dendritic cells showed early CTLA-4 upregulation as they became IL-10-producing regulatory-like cells; in vitro, not UC.

quote: Ten of the likely effector genes, including TGFB1 (transforming growth factor beta 1), FGF18 (fibroblast growth factor 18), CTSK (cathepsin K), and IL11 (interleukin 11), have therapeutics approved or in clinical trials, with mechanisms of action supportive of evaluation for efficacy in osteoarthritis.
summary: CTSK is one of several likely effector genes from an osteoarthritis GWAS with existing therapeutics; no UC data.

quote: Using Ctsk(-/-) mice, the authors demonstrate a protective role of cathepsin K against chronic DSS colitis.
summary: Cathepsin K-deficient mice develop worse chronic DSS colitis, and rectal recombinant cathepsin K ameliorates it, so cathepsin K has antibacterial, protective activity in the gut.

quote: We found that the anti-osteoclastic and anti-resorptive activities of Umb are mediated via suppression of the RANKL-induced Akt-c-Fos-NFATc1 signaling pathway and the attenuation of osteoclast-specific genes, such as TRAP, OSCAR, ATP6v0d2, and CtsK.
summary: CtsK is one of several osteoclast genes reduced by umbelliferone in a bone-loss study; no gut or UC data.

quote: Consistently, lymphokine like RANKL was uninvolved in CCL25-induced osteoclastogenesis; however, this manifestation was regulated by osteoclastic factors such as RANK, cathepsin K (CTSK), and TNF-α.
summary: CTSK is named among osteoclastic factors regulating CCL25-induced osteoclastogenesis in rheumatoid arthritis; no gene-specific result and no UC data.
